name: Ukiyo-e
summary: Japanese woodblock prints and paintings of the Edo city: a firm black contour, flat fields of colour, bold cropping and a high or tilted viewpoint. A team of artist, carver and printer makes each sheet, and publishers sell it to a mass market.

philosophy.core_thesis: A picture is a printed sheet in which the contour, the flat colour and the cropped viewpoint carry everything, and the moment is as fleeting as the city.
design_principles: Draw each form with a clean contour of uniform thickness, 1–2mm on a print of 25cm, and fill it with flat colour.
Set the horizon high, or tilt the ground plane up, so that the picture reads as a layered map and not as a box of space.
Cut figures and objects at the edge on purpose: a close foreground form fills 20–40% of the width.
Print the sky as a gradation (bokashi) from deep colour at the edge to white at the horizon, in a band of 15–25% of the height.
Use 4–8 flat colours and let the paper show as white; shade is a pattern or a line, not a blend.
Put a framed text cartouche, a title block and a signature seal in a corner, as part of the layout.
Fill planes of cloth, water and ground with repeated pattern: waves, rain lines, fabric motifs.
anti_patterns: Modelled shading with a smooth gradient on figures
Cast shadows and linear perspective with a low horizon
Painterly brush texture or visible canvas
Colour blending that hides the edge between two colour fields
Realistic anatomy with muscle and bone modelling
A central, symmetric, fully contained composition

composition.layout: Stacked horizontal bands (foreground, middle, sky), or a strong diagonal that cuts the sheet; forms overlap in flat layers.
composition.focal_point: A single accent of the strongest colour or contrast, placed off-centre at 1/3 to 2/5 from one side.
composition.format: Oban 25 by 38cm (landscape 3:2) or a vertical diptych of 2:3; the figure may be cropped by the edge.

principles.rule: Leave 20–40% of the sheet as empty colour field or white paper, usually as sky, mist or water.
Use a foreground form, such as a branch, a bridge rail or a pole, to cut across 10–30% of the sheet and frame the view.
Show depth by overlap and by band, with 3 flat planes and no vanishing point drawn to a rule.
Repeat a form (wave, pine, umbrella, rain line) 5–12 times with small changes in size and tilt.
Put the horizon line at 1/4 to 1/3 from the top, and the main form on a third line.

palette.strategy: A few flat, transparent water-based inks on white paper, with one strong blue and one warm colour; the key block in black.
palette.distribution: Paper white and pale ground 35–45%, mid colour fields 35–40%, the key black line and dark accents 10–15%, one saturated accent under 10%.
palette.ground: Warm white handmade paper (washi), which shows through as the lightest tone.

brushwork_and_medium.medium: Water-based pigment printed from carved cherry-wood blocks, one block for each colour, with a key block for the line.
brushwork_and_medium.support: Handmade washi paper, 25 by 38cm for an oban sheet.
brushwork_and_medium.brushwork: No brush trace shows. The line comes from the carved key block and has a uniform stroke of 1–2mm with a slight swell on curves.
brushwork_and_medium.paint_handling: Each colour is one flat, even layer; a second pass makes a darker tone; bokashi is wiped on the block by hand.
brushwork_and_medium.edges: Hard, crisp edges between colour fields, with a 0.5mm registration gap or overlap permitted.

light_and_modelling.light: No cast light source; the picture is lit evenly, as a flat diagram of the scene.
light_and_modelling.modelling: Pattern, line hatching and the change from one flat field to the next replace modelling; form is read from the contour.
light_and_modelling.shadow: Shadow is a flat darker tone or omitted; atmosphere shows as mist bands or bokashi at 20–40% of the height.
light_and_modelling.temperature: Cool blues for water and sky, warm ochre and red for figures and ground; the balance is by area, not by blend.

subject.typical: Courtesans and actors, travel stages, famous views, rain, snow and waves, birds and flowers, warriors and folk tales.
subject.figure_scale: Figures are small in landscape (5–15% of the height) and large in portraits (60–90%).
subject.treatment: Stylised faces by formula (a hooked nose, a slit eye), elegant poses, with movement in the line of the cloth.

surface.finish: Matt, with a slight emboss on the paper from the block pressure.
surface.texture: Visible paper fibre and fine wood grain in the large colour fields.

works.work: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (The Great Wave)

reference_works.note: Object ids were checked against the Met Open Access API (CC0) and the Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data). Look at the museum page for the image and its licence.

emotion.target_response: Poise and the passing moment: the viewer sees a clear, graphic image of an everyday scene, held for a second.

avoid_when: The brief asks for a photoreal or volumetric result.
The subject is a culture or a symbol outside Edo Japan, where the style would be a costume and not a language.

modifiers.how: Keep the flat fields and the cropped viewpoint; drop the paper texture and the carved line weight, and use vector shapes with 3–5 flat colours.
Keep the high horizon and the cropped foreground; replace the contour with visible strokes of 5–15mm and let the colour fields break into touches.
